title: EditPlan
description: Declarative description of a Premiere Pro timeline. Produced by the analysis engine, consumed by the UXP panel. This file is the ONLY contract between the two halves of the system.

timebase.description: Timebase of the OUTPUT sequence. Every `atFrame` and `durationFrames` in this document is expressed in this timebase.

presetPath.description: Absolute path to a .sqpreset. Omit to use createSequenceFromMedia and inherit from the first clip.

frameWidth.description: Set when an aspect was requested; the apply side needs it to compute the crop scale.

sections.description: The running order the editor described, in order. Optional; absent when no description was given.

candidates.description: Alternates the editor can swap into a slot. Optional: a plan without it loads and builds exactly as before, and the panel simply offers no swaps.

warnings.description: Non-fatal issues the editor should see in the panel before applying.

messageKey.description: Identity of the warning, e.g. 'music.stopsEarly'. The panel renders this in the editor's language and falls back to `message` when it has no translation, so `message` stays required.

params.description: Numbers the message is built from, for re-rendering in another language.

mediaRef.description: A source file. Deliberately stores relPath + hash and NEVER an absolute path, so the same EditPlan resolves on a local drive today and a NAS tomorrow. `root` names which configured folder relPath hangs off.

id.description: Derived from the filename. Constrained by what is structurally unsafe -- no whitespace, no path separators -- rather than by script: the old ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ rejected every Japanese-named clip, and enumerating scripts instead would simply have failed on the next language.

root.description: Which configured root relPath is relative to. 'music' is a separate library folder outside the footage; still a root and still not an absolute path, so the NAS move stays a settings change.

hash.description: sha256 of the first+last 4MiB plus size. Identity, not integrity.

role.description: Recipe-defined, e.g. cam-a, cam-b, mic-host, broll, music.

speaker.description: For isolated-mic recordings, the speaker on this channel.

width.description: Source pixel width; the apply side needs it to compute crop scale.

proxyPath.description: Absolute path to a proxy the panel should attach to this item. Absolute, unlike relPath, because a proxy is a local build artefact in the work cache rather than something under a configured root that should survive a move to shared storage.

clipEntry.description: One clip on the timeline. `inSeconds`/`outSeconds` are source time; `atFrame`/`durationFrames` are sequence time. Positions are explicit integer frames so a 200-cut assembly cannot accumulate float drift.

videoTrack.description: 0-based. -1 for an audio-only clip such as a music bed.

audioTrack.description: 0-based. -1 for a clip placed without audio.

reason.description: Human-readable justification, shown in the panel. Editors will not trust cuts they cannot interrogate.

sectionId.description: Groups entries so the editor can toggle a whole section off before applying.

fadeInFrames.description: Audio crossfade at the head. Non-zero on every join prevents clicks.

mogrt.description: Key into brandkit/mogrts.json, NOT a path.

fields.description: Field name -> value. Resolved to zero-based param indices at apply time via the brandkit param map.

matchName.description: Premiere component matchName, e.g. AE.ADBE Lumetri

transcript.description: Word-level transcript, pushed into Premiere via Transcript.createImportTextSegmentsAction so the assembled cut lines up with native Text-Based Editing.

languageConfidence.description: How sure the transcriber was, when the language was detected rather than stated. Absent when the editor named it. A wrong guess produces a fluent and meaningless transcript, so this is shown rather than acted on silently.

candidateEntry.description: A usable span the analyser found, offered to the editor as an alternate for a timeline slot. Carries no position: it is a span of a source, and the panel trims it to the length of whichever slot it is swapped into. The pool includes spans that were placed -- a shot already on the timeline is a valid alternate elsewhere, and a different moment of it is often the swap that is wanted.

score.description: The analyser's quality score, same scale as clip confidence. Orders the alternates; does not gate them.

reason.description: Why the analyser rated it as it did, shown beside the alternate.

sectionId.description: Which story section this span belongs to, when the job has one. Absent otherwise, in which case the panel groups by source instead.

thumbPath.description: Absolute path to a still from this span. Absolute, unlike relPath, because it is a cache artefact and not media the editor owns. Absent when thumbnails were not built.

sectionEntry.description: A named part of the edit, in running order. When the editor described the video, each described shot is one of these and `text` is what they actually wrote -- which is the only place that survives, since sectionId is a slug and loses words.

id.description: Matches the sectionId on timeline entries.

weight.description: Share of the running time, relative to the other sections.

matched.description: How many shots the footage supplied. Zero means the section is in the plan and not on the timeline.
